comparisons.peer_topic: Geopolitical and Consumer Protection Legal Risks
comparisons.peer_summary: Russian courts have entered judgments against the Firm totaling more than its onshore assets, including a $439 million judgment, and ordered interim asset freezes; the Firm appeals these decisions, warning that further enforcement could lead to full seizure of assets in Russia. In December 2024, the CFPB filed a complaint alleging insufficient fraud prevention efforts on the Zelle network by JPMorgan Chase and other banks, to which the defendants intend to respond.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America (BAC) and JPMorgan Chase (JPM) disclosed the same specific legal event: a December 2024 lawsuit filed by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) against them and other financial institutions regarding the processing of electronic payments on the Zelle network. BAC details that the CFPB alleges violations of the Consumer Financial Protection Act and the Electronic Fund Transfer Act related to fraud protection and disputed transfer investigations. Similarly, JPM discloses that the CFPB filed a complaint in the U.S. District Court for the District of Arizona alleging that it and its co-defendants failed to take sufficient efforts to prevent fraud on the Zelle network. Both disclosures identify the same regulatory actor, the same specific payment network (Zelle), and the same core allegation concerning inadequate fraud prevention.

sentences.text: On December 20, 2024, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) filed suit against BANA, JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., Wells Fargo Bank, N.A., and Early Warning Services, LLC in the U.S. District Court for the District of Arizona with respect to BANA's and co-defendants' processing of electronic payments of funds through the Zelle network.

The CFPB alleges that BANA and its co-defendants violated the Consumer Financial Protection Act by not adequately protecting consumers from fraud on the Zelle network and the Electronic Fund Transfer Act by not reasonably investigating and reimbursing disputed Zelle transfers, and seeks both monetary and injunctive relief.

In December 2024, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ("CFPB") filed a complaint against Early Warning Services, LLC ("EWS"), Bank of America, N.A., Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. and JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. in the United States District Court for the District of Arizona.
The CFPB alleges that EWS and the defendant banks have failed to take sufficient efforts to prevent fraud on the Zelle network.
